newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PAKISTAN NEW CROP COTTON RATES DIP AS RAINS STOP.
newsitem.headline: PAKISTAN NEW CROP COTTON RATES DIP AS RAINS STOP.

text.p: Prices of cotton from Pakistan's new 1997/98 (July-June) crop dipped on Wednesday after rains stopped in Sindh province and dealers said arrival of fresh supplies would improve in the coming days.

"After recent rains and continued cloudy weather, there is again bright sunlight which is good for the crop," dealer Kishan Chand said. "Expectations that the cotton supply will increase in the coming days has dragged down prices."
Chand said the mills were on the buying side on reports that bad weather could delay new arrivals in Punjab province.
In the kerb, new-crop NIAB-78 variety was traded around 2,230 rupees ($54.89) per maund (37.32 k.g).
